Quick note from LaunchPad — we have a hard date for our EU + US feature release on June 22. Traffic spike profile attached (launch_traffic_model.xlsx). Our backend will fan out to your generation API for personalization and similarity calls. We expect a 10x traffic jump in the first 48 hours (~3.2M tokens/day peak) and sustained 2x for the following week.

Can Redwood provision a short-term rate-limit/quota exception and advise if we should be on Hosted or request a short Dedicated pool? We're flexible — main asks are:
- Temporary soft limit increase to 12k rps aggregate for 48 hours
- Priority routing or pre-warm/cache guidance
- A contact for 24–48h monitoring during launch

I've attached our forecast and a completed requested_quota_form.pdf. If helpful, we can hop on a 30-min sync this week.

Thanks — appreciate it,
Ava

Jonas — thanks for flagging. Quick initial read: forecast seems realistic and fits the spike profile we've planned for, but 12k rps aggregate is outside the default burst window for Hosted for an account at their tier. Options and trade-offs:

1) Short-term quota exception on Hosted (preferred operationally):
   - Provision +40% soft quota for 48h with hard caps and automated rollback. We can add traffic-based throttling to avoid tail latency. Needs product approval and a signed transient SLA addendum.
   - Risk: if they exceed forecast by >20% we can still hit contention; we'll auto-failover to a compatible smaller model to preserve availability.

2) Move to a temporary Dedicated pool for 72h:
   - Highest predictability and isolated GPU capacity. Lead time ~8 hours to allocate if capacity available. Costly for customer; requires billing sign-off.

3) Hybrid: keep Hosted but use routing policy to send 25% of traffic to Dedicated warm nodes (if we can spin them) to smooth peak.

Needs from Sales/Product:
- Signed acknowledgement of transient quota/exception (we'll draft)
- A runbook for escalation and a primary PagerDuty contact
- Confirm which model variants they will hit — we should pre-validate model size to optimize kernel selection

I can own the Hosted exception path if Product signs off; I'll need final approval by EOD June 19 to schedule changes and SRE monitoring shifts.

-Neha

Ava — thanks for the forecast and patience. Quick summary and next steps (agreed internally):

1) Technical approach: We will provision a Hosted transient quota exception equivalent to +35% of their current aggregate quota for a rolling 48-hour window starting at their chosen launch time. If traffic exceeds the forecast by >25% we will automatically route degraded requests to a smaller model to preserve availability. Neha will own the rollout.

2) Contingency: If LaunchPad prefers guaranteed isolation we can spin up a temporary Dedicated pool (72h). Karthik will offer a one-time credit (up to $15k) to subsidize Dedicated if needed.

3) Ops & monitoring: Primary PagerDuty contact: Neha (SRE rotation), secondary: Laura. We'll stand up a dedicated Slack channel for the launch and a lightweight dashboard (INF-6742).

4) Paperwork: We'll send a short transient-SLA addendum and a launch-readiness checklist — please sign the acknowledgement by June 19 to lock change windows.

5) Timeline: please confirm your exact launch start time (UTC) so we can schedule the quota window and pre-warm actions.

Linking the Jira runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-6742 and shared Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/launchpad-preflight.

Next: Karthik will send the credit acknowledgement; Neha will prepare the Hosted change plan and rollback. I'll schedule a 20-min prelaunch check on June 21 (11am PT) unless you prefer a different slot.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch.

-Jonas Weber
